reason: The cited evidence shows that refractory high-entropy alloys can have high-temperature strength and ductility (E1, E3) and that pure tungsten has poor toughness (E2), but none of the passages specifically address the equimolar WTaTiVZr alloy, its grain boundary cohesion, lattice distortion, or a direct comparison of its plastic strain and toughness to pure tungsten. The key mechanistic premises are therefore largely unsupported by the cited evidence.
premises: Refractory elements provide solid solution strengthening and lattice distortion in RHEAs
Grain boundary cohesion is enhanced in the equimolar WTaTiVZr alloy
These mechanisms improve plastic strain and toughness over pure tungsten
The alloy's composition avoids high-activation elements like Nb, Mo, Cr, Ni
Prior RHEAs show high-temperature strength and ductility (e.g., 300–400 MPa at 1000°C)
